filename: Data-Driven Integration Kernels for Interpretable Nonlocal Operator Learning(1).pdf
title: Data-driven integration kernels for interpretable nonlocal operator learning
testbed_rationale: Uses publicly available cloud-optimized datasets (LEAP ARCO-ERA5 and Planetary Computer IMERG) along with open-source Zenodo code to establish an offline parameterization testbed for precipitation from thermodynamic profiles.
pain_points: Nonlocal ML models typically encode spatial/vertical/temporal dependencies implicitly in large parameter sets, hindering interpretability and risking overfitting as nonlocal context expands.
Post-hoc explainability methods (XAI) yield sample-dependent attributions that compound uncertainty and can be hard to interpret physically.
Strong inter-variable correlations in atmospheric data can cause unconstrained/nonparametric kernels to be underdetermined.
extraction_notes: The paper focuses on South Asian monsoon precipitation parameterization (5–25°N, 60–90°E) for June–August (2000–2020), partitioned chronologically: 2000–2014 training, 2015–2017 validation, 2018–2020 testing.
